question: Q1

solver_equivalence.claim: the vectorised solver reproduces the validated cell-centred implementation (baseline role B2)
solver_equivalence.metric: max abs difference of the reported profile

scheme_independence.claim: the sensitivity sweep runs on the baseline implementation but describes the model, not the scheme
scheme_independence.metric: max abs difference of the reported moisture profile at t = 1800 s, sweep implementation vs main role M2
scheme_independence.interpretation: the sweep implementation and the main role agree to within one unit in the last reported decimal

h_m_perturbation.claim: the reported moisture field, given h_m = 8e-7 m/s as supplied in appendix 2
h_m_perturbation.perturbation: h_m scaled by 0.95 / 1.05 / 1.10 (the value is a problem input, not fitted)
h_m_perturbation.metric: max abs change of the 5 reported moisture values at t = 1800 s
h_m_perturbation.threshold: predeclared: < 1e-4 (one unit in the last reported decimal) would be negligible
h_m_perturbation.interpretation: a 5 percent change in h_m moves the surface value by ~0.035 kg/kg (2.3 percent), 350+ units in the last decimal; the reported surface value is meaningful only under the supplied h_m

D_perturbation.metric: max abs change of reported moisture
D_perturbation.interpretation: second-order parameter effect, about half the h_m effect

mass_equation_form.claim: the mass equation uses the Fick form given by the problem (decision g_assumption_mass_equation_form)
mass_equation_form.perturbation: the wet-basis self-consistent form, whose effective diffusivity is (1+C) times larger
mass_equation_form.metric: max abs change of the reported moisture field
mass_equation_form.interpretation: the alternative form changes the surface value by an order of magnitude more than the reported precision; the adopted reading is per the problem text and is recorded as a conditional limitation

environment_interpolation.claim: linear interpolation of attachment 1, including t = 100 s which is not a sample point
environment_interpolation.perturbation: cubic spline interpolation instead of linear
environment_interpolation.metric: max abs change of the reported moisture field

end_face_neglect.perturbation: not a numerical perturbation; magnitude estimate of the ignored axial transport
end_face_neglect.metric: axial penetration depth over the Q1 window and the end-face share of the transfer area
end_face_neglect.interpretation: over the 1800 s window the axial mass penetration is under 2 percent of the length, so the radial assumption is well supported for Q1; it degrades for the multi-day questions

numerical_discretisation.claim: the reported four-decimal values are grid- and solver-tolerance-independent in both roles
numerical_discretisation.perturbation: main: grid 400 vs 800 nodes, BDF rtol 1e-8 vs 1e-9; baseline: grid 400 vs 800 cells, dt 0.5 vs 0.25 s
numerical_discretisation.metric: max abs change of the reported profile

independent_implementation.claim: the reported values are reproduced by an independently written solver
independent_implementation.perturbation: different spatial discretisation and adaptive BDF time integration
independent_implementation.metric: difference of the Richardson limits at the hardest point (r = 2.0 cm, t = 100 s)

output_degeneracy.claim: the outputs are not degenerate or concentrated
output_degeneracy.interpretation: all of the sensitivity lives in the surface column because the interior has not responded within 1800 s

limitations: h_m and D are problem-supplied inputs, not fitted quantities; the reported values are conditional on them
the interior moisture is essentially unchanged over the 1800 s window, so Q1 cannot discriminate between competing long-time diffusivity models
the axial end faces are ignored; the estimate above bounds the effect for Q1 but not for the multi-day questions

fallback_trigger_relevance.trigger: M2 and B2 disagree beyond the reported tolerance and the disagreement cannot be attributed
